varieties.name: MO1015 (proposed commercial name "Carla")
varieties.traits: Large, Waltham-shaped, smooth dark tan skin; fresh-market/export segment; average fruit 1.6-1.8kg in trials
varieties.note: A Starke Ayres breeding-trial line specifically framed as new butternut options for Western Cape growers, aimed at the export fresh-market segment rather than a home garden. Named here as the only zone-specific butternut lead found, not as a general recommendation.

evidence.quote: MO 1015 and MO 1014 identified as having exceptional potential to satisfy the demands of the export sector. MO1015 (proposed name Carla) is a large, Waltham-shaped, fresh market segment variety with a smooth, dark tan-coloured skin that produced an average fruit size of 1.6-1.8kg in the trials.
evidence.doc: New butternut squash varieties for the Western Cape, Starke Ayres news article (via search snippet — page could not be independently re-fetched for a verbatim quote in this pass)

gaps: Starke Ayres' own Butternut Production Guideline 2019 (fetched and read in full, https://www.starkeayres.com/uploads/files/Squash/Butternut/Butternut-Production-Guideline-2019.pdf) names NO specific cultivars at all — it is generic agronomy (spacing, fertiliser, climate) and matches what crop-catalog.ts already cites for spacing.

No zone-by-zone butternut variety table was found for any of the other 7 zones. The widely-known OP 'Waltham Butternut' type sold by several SA home-garden retailers was considered but not added, because no South African primary/seed-company source was opened and quoted for it in this pass (would have been inserted from general knowledge, which the brief forbids).

This matches crop-catalog.ts's own existing stance on butternut: it deliberately carries NO varieties array, with a header comment stating published SA guidance here is 'purely about sow-timing' rather than a real region-driven variety choice — this file's single Western Cape lead is a genuine addition, not a reversal of that finding, and the other 7 zones remain a gap consistent with that prior conclusion.
